A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Image Diffusion Preview with Consistency Solver. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and editing experiments, human and LLM-based preview evaluations, and solver, reward, and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds cross-model transfer experiments and hardware-dependent latency analysis.

M1.justification: The timestep-conditioned MLP, weighted multistep update in Eq. (5), PPO objective, and default solver configuration are unchanged. Cross-model experiments apply the existing solver without retraining; they introduce no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use LAION, COCO 2017, GenEval, and KontextBench for the same generation, editing, and preview-evaluation tasks. The additional diffusion backbones and hardware configurations do not change the represented datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained generation, editing, qualitative, and satisfaction comparisons. The new transfer evaluation reuses previously evaluated DDIM, iPNDM, DEIS, and Multistep DPM rather than introducing another baseline method.

E3.justification: v2 adds a transfer protocol applying the SD1.5-trained solver without retraining, including 5-step SD1.4 and 10-step SDXL evaluations. Appendix E additionally compares H100, M4, and CPU latency with and without an assumed 300 ms reaction time per trial. These substantially extend the evaluation settings while retaining the original protocols.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix F add quantitative and qualitative tests of transfer across diffusion models. Appendix E adds analysis of how hardware and user-reaction overhead affect preview efficiency. The existing architecture, solver-order, and reward ablations are retained; moving the latter two to Tables S2–S3 adds no new ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across independent experimental runs. Existing participant counts and stochastic training-rollout information are unchanged, and the added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Original benchmark, satisfaction, and ablation values are retained. New Table 4 reports SDXL FID 23.32 versus Multistep DPM's 26.32 at 10 steps, and SD1.4 FID 20.22 versus 25.22 at 5 steps. Table S4 adds hardware- and reaction-time-dependent latency results, Figure S2 adds transfer examples, and Table 5 adds speedup summaries to existing timing results.

T1.justification: Equation (4) corrects the j-dependent step-size prefactor outside the derivative sum to the current interval, t_(i+1) minus t_i. The proposed solver equation and appendix Taylor-expansion and solver-equivalence derivations otherwise remain unchanged apart from numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same preview-and-refine framework and RL-trained solver claims. The headline claims of 47% fewer steps and nearly 50% less interaction time are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new transfer results as suggesting shared optimal sampling dynamics across diffusion models. Appendix E also qualifies efficiency gains: reaction overhead reduces speedup on H100, while slower hardware makes that overhead relatively negligible. Existing ablation interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds M4 and Platinum 8480 CPU hardware identification and the 300 ms timing-accounting assumption. The original training recipe, including 3,000 iterations, learning rate 0.0001, and approximately 12 H100 GPU hours, and the code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Amano et al. (2006) on human visual perception to support the reaction-time assumption. The positioning relative to diffusion solvers and distillation is unchanged. EditScore, EditReward, and other bibliographic revisions concern retained works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and heading edits, renames high-quality mode to full mode, updates affiliation/contact information, and adds acknowledgments. Section 5.5 is shortened while its detailed ablation discussion moves to Appendix D.5–D.6; most original prose and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and S4 and Figure S2, reorganizes the timing table with a speedup column, and relocates the solver-order and reward tables to the appendix. Figure 4 is repositioned and supplemental items are renumbered. The original method diagrams and principal benchmark-table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens applicability evidence through cross-model transfer tests and improves the interpretation of practical latency by accounting for hardware and assumed reaction overhead. It also corrects Eq. (4) while retaining the original results and ablations. These are useful incremental gains; the reaction-time analysis assumes 300 ms rather than measuring actual interaction time, limiting how fully it validates the practical speedup claim.
